mappings.note: Persistence of the image on the retina is a fact about how the eye works, and the eye is named verbatim in LO-174; not LO-170, no optical phenomenon outside the eye being explained.
Rods as the cells sensitive to light intensity is eye structure and function; not LO-166, which is used where rods and cones are contrasted.
Cones as the colour-sensitive cells is eye structure and function; grouped with the rods item.
A hazy or opaque lens identified as cataract relates a symptom to the condition behind it; not LO-174, because a disorder rather than normal anatomy is named.
The equality of the angles of incidence and reflection is the angle outcome named verbatim in LO-172; not LO-170, which covers image formation rather than the angles.
The nature of a plane-mirror image explains image formation; not LO-166, no two mirror types being contrasted.
What reflection is explains the phenomenon; not LO-172, no angles involved.
Dispersion as the splitting of light explains a phenomenon; not LO-167, nothing being classified.
Excluding what is not a light source sorts objects into luminous and non-luminous; not LO-170, no phenomenon explained.
Choosing the mirror that gives a virtual, laterally inverted, same-size image differentiates mirror types by their behaviour; not LO-170, a mirror rather than the image being asked for.
The angle between incident ray and normal being the angle of incidence is LO-172's own subject; not LO-170, the angle rather than the image.
The eye lens being convex is eye structure; grouped with the other eye-anatomy items.
A kaleidoscope working by multiple reflections is the formation of multiple images LO-170 names verbatim; not LO-175, no model being constructed.
Infinite images between two parallel mirrors is the formation of multiple images verbatim; grouped with the kaleidoscope item.
Eye colour arising from the iris is eye structure; grouped with the eye-anatomy items.
The incident ray named as the beam striking the surface belongs to the explanation of reflection; not LO-172, no angle being measured.
The reflected ray named as the beam bounced back belongs to the same explanation; grouped with the incident-ray item.
The cornea as the bulging front of the eyeball is eye structure; grouped with the eye-anatomy items.
Braille letting visually impaired people read and write is science applied in daily life; not LO-174, an aid rather than anatomy.
The iris regulating light entering the eye is eye structure and function; grouped with the eye-anatomy items.
Ciliary muscles changing the lens's focal length is eye structure and function; grouped with the eye-anatomy items.
The retina as where the image forms is eye structure and function; grouped with the eye-anatomy items.
The far point of a normal eye is a fact about normal vision; not LO-169, no defect being traced.
The least distance of distinct vision is a fact about normal vision; grouped with the far-point item.
The near point at sixty describes how normal vision changes with age; grouped with the other vision-range items.
The optic nerve carrying the message to the brain is eye structure and function; grouped with the eye-anatomy items.
Inability to see distant objects identified as myopia relates a symptom to the defect causing it; not LO-174, a disorder rather than normal anatomy.
Inability to see near objects identified as hypermetropia is the mirror case; coded with the myopia item.
A shining surface that rebounds light being a mirror belongs to the explanation of reflection; not LO-166, no mirror types contrasted.
The incident ray named as the beam striking the surface belongs to the explanation of reflection; duplicate in substance of the earlier item.
The band of seven colours being the spectrum explains dispersion; not LO-167, nothing being classified.
The cornea as the bulging front of the eyeball is eye structure; duplicate in substance of the earlier cornea item.
Choosing the correct statement about rods and cones contrasts the two cell types on structure and function; not LO-174, which is used where a single part is named.
The relation between the angles of incidence and reflection is LO-172's own subject; duplicate in substance of the earlier angle item.
Which mirror serves as a backview mirror is choosing a device for everyday use; not LO-166, a use rather than a bare comparison of mirrors.
Braille letting visually impaired people read and write is science applied in daily life; duplicate in substance of the earlier Braille item.
Contrasting the camera's real image with the microscope's virtual one differentiates image types; not LO-170, two instruments being compared rather than one phenomenon explained.
Working out the angle of incidence when incident and reflected rays are at ninety degrees is measurement of those angles, LO-172 verbatim; not LO-170, an angle rather than an image.
Dispersion as the splitting of white light explains a phenomenon; duplicate in substance of the earlier dispersion item.
The defect behind not seeing distant objects clearly relates a symptom to its cause; duplicate in substance of the myopia item.
